summary: The universal upper tradeoff function of Theorem A.7 is undefined at an admissible positive-KL point. The standard-deviation sample complexity is also incorrect; foundational bounds survive.
limitations: No empirical reproduction; code and optional OpenReview attachments unavailable.
Conjectures4.4/7.2 unresolved; scoped mathematical checks do not certify the entire paper.

problems.claim: A.7 defines a universal upper tradeoff function.
problems.check: D2=.130812>0; DU(tau)<0 for all tau>1 by log(tau)<=tau-1.
problems.result: Required function value does not exist.
problems.counterevidence: Basic inequalities survive; figure bound is distinct conjecture; branch restriction changes the theorem.
problems.impact: General Section7 theoretical tradeoff guarantee invalid as specified.

independent_verification.source_and_assumptions: Independently checked physical pp3,8,19 and viewed p19. Assumptions 2.1-2.2 permit a single prompt with two equiprobable distinct-reward outcomes; no low-mass restriction occurs in A.7.
independent_verification.decisive_reasoning: For S=1/2, D_U(t)=log(t)-(t-1)/t-t(t-1). Since log(t)<=t-1, D_U(t)<0 for all t>1, whereas the actual n=2 KL is (1/4)log(1/2)+(3/4)log(3/2)>0. Definition 7.1 requires evaluation at this KL, so the stated function is undefined there.
independent_verification.alternative_and_dependency: A parametric inequality at sample counts is not a function on all required KL values. Truncating to a branch or completing with 1 changes the theorem. This invalidates the universal Section7 tradeoff guarantee while Theorems3.1/3.4/5.3 remain logically independent.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Major retained for a core theoretical guarantee. No full repair; no inference of empirical invalidity.

problems.claim: M=O(log n log(1/delta)) controls standard deviation.
problems.counterevidence: Uniform case deterministic; confidence is different from precision.

independent_verification.source_and_assumptions: Independently checked p4 Eq24, p5 text following Lemma4.5, and p3 finite-support/distinct-reward assumptions. The statement explicitly concerns standard deviation, not failure probability.
independent_verification.decisive_reasoning: For n=2 and masses(.9,.1), selected probabilities are(.81,.19). Recomputed d values and variance below. Positive fixed variance gives sd(mean)=sqrt(var/M), requiring M>=var/delta^2, which cannot be logarithmic in 1/delta.
independent_verification.alternative_and_dependency: Uniform masses give deterministic estimates but do not cover the nonuniform counterexample. A tail-confidence reinterpretation does not match the printed precision claim.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Minor retained for ancillary precision statement; estimator and conjectured bias bound are unaffected. Popoviciu applied to [0,B_n] gives the stated sufficient B_n^2/(4 delta^2) bound, not a bias guarantee.
